title: Design and Integration of Chassis and Power-train for a Range Extended Electric Vehicle
summary: A two-seater academic REEV study connecting electric propulsion with an engine-generator range extender. FYP-1 established the architecture and integration methodology.
overview: Range anxiety and limited charging access motivate this two-seater academic project at Air University. The selected series architecture keeps the wheels electrically driven: the battery supplies a controller and traction motor, while a petrol engine runs a generator to support or recharge the electrical system when required. The engine has no direct mechanical connection to the wheels.
approach: Reviewed electric, hybrid and range-extended vehicle literature to establish the problem and compare architectures.
Selected a series REEV architecture and identified the battery, motor, controller, generator, fuel tank and DC/DC converter.
Developed the sizing and integration methodology, including a power-flow block diagram and a conceptual battery-state-of-charge operating sequence.
Defined a development path from design calculations and component sizing to chassis integration and vehicle demonstration.
components: Petrol engine and generator range extender
DC/DC converter for auxiliary electrical loads
outcomes: FYP-1 is complete: literature review, architecture selection, component identification and methodology form the present deliverable.
FYP-2 is the next phase for design calculations and component sizing.
The final vehicle is planned for FYP-3. The supplied vehicle rendering is a concept illustration, and no completed-vehicle range is claimed.
